newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent stagnates at higher levels in dead marke.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent stagnates at higher levels in dead marke.

text.p: IPE Brent futures stagnated at higher levels achieved in early trade at midday on Monday in an extremely quiet market dominated by spread plays ahead of the May contract's expiry on Tuesday, traders said.
May Brent was trading 20 cents higher at $18.10 a barrel at 1157 GMT, while the June contract was 21 cents stronger at $18.28.
"Most of the action's been on the spreads," said one trader. "Without that it would have been dead. I thinks it's the quietest day since New Year's Eve. People are sitting around reading the paper."

Traders attributed some of the earlier gains to news that U.S and Saudi Arabian intelligence officers had linked a senior Iranian government official to Shiite Moslems suspected of the 1996 bombing of Khobar U.S. military compound in Saudi Arabia.
But many players said they were waiting to see how NYMEX reacted to the story before making any moves.
"No-one's going to do anything very drastic until they see how New York reacts," one trader said.
Meanwhile, last week's EU-Iran spat appeared to have drifted into the background, although traders were keeping a close eye on further developments.

On the technical front, few players saw the market making an assault on a ridge of stubborn resistance around the downside gap left on the charts between April 2 and 3, spanning $18.40 to $18.50 for May and $18.62 to $18.77 for June in Monday's session.
But some chartists said a positive follow through of a supportive double bottom seen on NYMEX crude charts at $18.96 on April 4 and 10 would probably boost Brent.
